subject: sociology
title: Functionalism in Education: Durkheim's Role
welcome_lead: Durkheim says education makes us social — and skilled.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology functionalism education Durkheim social solidarity specialist skills.
final_note: Education holds society together and trains its workers.

concepts.def: Sense of belonging to a society.
Shared values and beliefs of society.
Modern division of labour requires specific training.

walkthroughs.body_html: Durkheim (1925): school transmits society's culture — history, language, religion — creating social solidarity. Children learn to subordinate desires to group rules. Society in miniature: relationships with teachers and peers prepare for adult relationships with strangers.

Modern organic solidarity rests on division of labour. Education trains workers in specific skills — Durkheim noted increasingly specialised curricula. Pre-industrial mechanical solidarity needed only shared culture; industrial society needs interdependent specialists.

UK National Curriculum carries Durkheim's logic — shared content for solidarity, specialist STEM/vocational tracks for skills. Critique: doesn't ask whose values are transmitted (Marxists) or whether all learn equally (interactionists). Still influential in education policy debate.
